request.label: admins-digest-intro
request.system: You write short, plain, honest prose for a Business Central administrator audience about the Business Central launch event. Use only the facts given. No em-dashes, no bullet lists, no headings, no hype words. Return JSON { "text": "..." } with paragraphs separated by blank lines.
request.prompt:
Write the introduction (3 short paragraphs, 120 to 180 words total) of a "administrator digest" about the 2026 release wave 2 launch event, for Business Central administrators (you run the tenants: admin center, updates, permissions, security, environments, telemetry). Tone: direct, a bit of humor, no corporate fluff, no hype adjectives, no em-dashes. Say what themes dominate for this audience and what to watch first. Use only the feature list below; do not add facts. Status rule for this event: a feature is generally available unless the presenters said otherwise; "(implied)" means nothing was said, so treat those as GA and never use the word implied. Do not list features one by one, the list follows your text. Do not use headings.

Features selected for this audience (51, about 64 minutes of video):
- Microsoft Copilot chat in Business Central (GA, 12 min, Copilot and agents): A unified Microsoft Copilot chat opens from the Copilot button in Business Central, replacing the old Copilot UI. It reasons over Business Central data within the user's permissions and context, with progress messages, tables and citations.
- AI policy compliance check (GA (implied), 5 min, Expense Agent): An admin setting lets AI check expenses against policies configured per expense category, and flag non-compliant or unclear items for the approver. It can use Copilot credits.
- Early install of hotfixes for Microsoft apps (GA (implied), 3 min, Admin and platform): Customers can install a prepared hotfix version of a Microsoft app immediately or in the next update window from the app details page. It bypasses safe deployment, so use it only when the version fixes an issue that affects the customer.
- PTE lifecycle management in the admin center (GA (implied), 3 min, Admin and platform): Upload, install and update operations are added to PTE management in the admin center, bringing full PTE lifecycle management into one place. Installs start from the apps page with an install extension button.
- Multiple scheduled PTE installs and cancel (GA (implied), 3 min, Admin and platform): Several future installs can be scheduled for the same PTE, for example one version on the next minor and another on the next major update. Scheduled installs show on the app details page and can be canceled before they run.
- Cross-environment master data management (GA (implied), 2 min, Integration (Fabric, Shopify, MDM)): Subsidiaries in other environments of the same tenant can pull master data from the HQ company. It is built in, with no middleware or custom code, and uses the same UI as same-environment synchronization.
- Flagged and compliant policy statuses (GA (implied), 2 min, Expense Agent): Reports and lines show compliant or flagged, with AI reasoning beside flagged expenses. Missing receipt info also flags a line.
- Index management access (GA (implied), 2 min, Admin and platform): The index management page can be found through Tell Me, including semantic search, and through a Manage indexes button on table information. Indexes, including SIFT indexes, can be disabled there.
- Presubmission policy check (GA (implied), 2 min, Expense Agent): Submitters can run the AI policy check manually with a check policies button before sending the report. It is not automatic for submitters and can be turned off to save AI credits.
- Business Central data questions (GA (implied), 2 min, Copilot and agents): Copilot searches Business Central data with the user's context, permissions and company, for example most urgent sales orders. It also analyzes sales data, such as the least sold items, and suggests actions.
- Export logs pushed to Fabric (preview, 2 min, Integration (Fabric, Shopify, MDM)): Synchronization logs are also written into Fabric for monitoring through the SQL endpoint.
- Database export as an environment operation (GA, 1 min, Admin and platform): An export appears on the operations page with status, times, who triggered it and the error on failure. It uses the same filters and details flyout as other operations.
- Change propagation and synchronization log (GA (implied), 1 min, Integration (Fabric, Shopify, MDM)): Source changes show in the subsidiary after about a minute. Logs and job rescheduling work as for single-environment sync.
- MCP server on/off toggle (GA (implied), 1 min, Admin and platform): A toggle on the Copilot and agent capabilities page activates or deactivates the MCP server as a whole.
- System fields in profiles (GA (implied), 1 min, Admin and platform): In the profile page designer, system fields can be found and added to a page. The example adds modified by to the sales order card for all profile users.
- Initial cross-environment synchronization (GA (implied), 1 min, Integration (Fabric, Shopify, MDM)): Start all runs default tables in a predefined order, starting with business relations and dimensions.
- Permission overview page in context (GA (implied), 1 min, Admin and platform): The permissions overview page can be opened from the permission sets list, the permission set card and the table information page.
- Quality inspection assignment and role-based control (GA (implied), 1 min, Supply chain): Changing a header field prompts self-assignment. Quality admin or supervisor roles can change quantities, reassign, reopen or delete finished inspections.
- Bookmarks in profiles (GA (implied), 1 min, Admin and platform): Bookmarked views can be added to a profile's role center for all its users.
- Operations page audit of PTE actions (GA (implied), 1 min, Admin and platform): The environment operations page captures every PTE install, update and scheduling action. Scheduled operations show a target app version and are reconciled to completed when the update starts.
- Free-text expense policies per category (GA (implied), 1 min, Expense Agent): Policies are free-text lines linked to expense categories, including custom ones. Each policy should be its own line.
- Feature switch for the new document experience (GA (implied), 1 min, Admin and platform): Feature management has a setting to enable or turn off the new document experience. This allows a gradual rollout of composite layouts per environment.
- Synchronization overview and details logs (preview, 1 min, Integration (Fabric, Shopify, MDM)): Overview and details logs are under monitoring with views for all, errors or pushed data.
- Server features box in MCP configuration (GA (implied), 1 min, Admin and platform): The MCP configuration page separates server features from APIs and shows which system tools each feature enables.
- Update a PTE from the admin center (GA (implied), 1 min, Admin and platform): From the app details page you can install a different version of an installed PTE. This triggers an update rather than a new install.
- Automatic revert after 72 hours (GA (implied), 1 min, Admin and platform): The environment reverts to a typical sandbox configuration after 72 hours. The revert happens in the first update window after that.
- Change log for financial report definitions (GA (implied), 1 min, Admin and platform): Change log is set up automatically on financial report definition tables, auditing changes with user ID.
- Deprecation of in-environment PTE management (announced, 1 min, Admin and platform): PTE management in the extension management pages and in the automation API will be deprecated as of version 30.0. Users should migrate to the admin center within about half a year and not mix both experiences in one environment.
- Telemetry for Open in Excel (GA (implied), 1 min, Admin and platform): A telemetry signal records who used Open in Excel and when.
- Copilot and agent capabilities admin control (GA (implied), 1 min, Admin and platform): The Copilot and agent capabilities page lets admins opt in or out of AI features and control who can use them.
- Feedback on Copilot responses (GA (implied), 1 min, Copilot and agents): Users can give thumbs up or down and share screenshots and prompts to help troubleshoot unexpected results.
- Match production configuration (GA (implied), 1 min, Admin and platform): Administrators can temporarily match a sandbox database configuration to a typical production database. This helps evaluate production behavior, for example for performance work or cloud migration.
- Database export reliability (GA, 1 min, Admin and platform): The most common failures were removed across the export pipeline, so fewer than 1% of exports fail. Big environments can be exported reliably.
- Export history API endpoint deprecated (GA (implied), 1 min, Admin and platform): The admin center API export history endpoint is deprecated and kept only on API versions 2.29 and earlier. Automations should move to the environment operations API.
- Deployment schedules for PTE installs (GA (implied), 1 min, Admin and platform): When installing a PTE you can choose immediate, next minor update or next major update, plus a sync mode. Previously in-product installs could only be immediate.
- App view filter for per tenant extensions (GA (implied), 1 min, Admin and platform): The apps page can be filtered to show different views of installed apps, for example only per tenant extensions.
- Copilot respects user permissions (GA (implied), 1 min, Admin and platform): Copilot runs as the signed-in user and accesses data only within their permissions.
- Pull-based incremental synchronization (GA (implied), 1 min, Integration (Fabric, Shopify, MDM)): HQ stays read-only and subsidiaries pull only the changes across environments.
- Permission set for HQ read access (GA (implied), 1 min, Admin and platform): A purpose-designed permission set with read access to default tables is assigned to the app user in the source.
- Policies pending after changes (GA (implied), 1 min, Expense Agent): Changing merchant or description resets the status to policies pending until re-evaluated.
- Single Export database button (GA (implied), 0 min, Admin and platform): Export database is now one button instead of a dropdown with export history. The flyout notes that progress can be tracked on the operations page.
- Entra app registration and consent (GA (implied), 0 min, Admin and platform): An Entra app with API read/write all permissions is registered and the HQ admin gives consent in Business Central.
- Database export history page retirement (announced, 0 min, Admin and platform): The database export history page is retiring. Its information, plus more, is on the operations page.
- Permission sets for Fabric integration (preview, 0 min, Admin and platform): Permission sets cover activation, administration and read-only configuration access.
- Match production in admin center API (GA (implied), 0 min, Admin and platform): The match production configuration operation is supported in the admin center APIs. Developers can automate it in their processes.
- Shared or per-subsidiary app registration (GA (implied), 0 min, Admin and platform): One app can be shared across subsidiaries or one registered per subsidiary, depending on audit needs.
- Match production operation tracking (GA (implied), 0 min, Admin and platform): The operation can be tracked like other admin center operations. Details show who started it and when.
- Match production usage limit (GA (implied), 0 min, Admin and platform): The operation is limited to three occurrences per tenant per calendar month, each lasting 72 hours.
- NST on .NET 10 (GA (implied), 0 min, Admin and platform): The Business Central service tier now runs on .NET 10.
- Restart warning flyout (GA (implied), 0 min, Admin and platform): The admin center button opens a flyout explaining the action and warning that the environment restarts. Connected users are disconnected.
- Match production paid license requirement (GA (implied), 0 min, Admin and platform): The feature is only available on tenants with a paid license type. This includes partners using the partner sandbox license.

output.text:
The theme for administrators this wave is that things moved house. Per tenant extension management now lives in the admin center, with upload, install, update, scheduled installs and an audit trail on the operations page. Database export became an environment operation too, and Copilot now has one chat, plus a capabilities page where you decide who gets what.

Check the deprecations first. PTE management in the extension management pages and the automation API will be deprecated as of version 30.0, so migrate to the admin center and do not mix both experiences in one environment. The admin center API export history endpoint stays only on versions 2.29 and earlier, and the export history page is retiring. Any script that touches either deserves a look.

After that, try the new switches, such as the MCP server toggle. Early hotfix install skips safe deployment, so keep it for fixes that matter to you. Match production is limited to three occurrences per tenant per month. Fabric export logs are still in preview.
